objective: Establish how pi's codemode works in pi 1.5.0 and what Moonshot says about Kimi K3.1 Pro reasoning effort, so the maintainer can decide how HolyAgent's pi root uses codemode and whether the root runs at max.
scope: Maintainer (verbatim): "I wanna specifically use codemode" and "assess if max is worth it for root". Context: /home/user/holyagent/docs/pi/orchestration.md and claude-parity.md describe builtin:codemode as the host for HolyAgent's workflow scripts (the root writes a JavaScript script that fans out specialists, like Claude Code's Workflow tool).

Codemode, from pi 1.5.0 docs and source (https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent@1.5.0/docs/ and the earendil-works/pi repository): its modes (for example whether an 'only' mode exposes every tool through codemode and what that breaks; rpiv-ask-user-question issue #310 says it is not invoked under codemode 'only'); which tools and extension tools a script can call and how (including tools from extensions such as pi-subagents and @aliou/pi-processes); whether a script can call a subagent or model and await or run several in parallel; PI_CODEMODE_MAX_WORKERS semantics (default 2, counted across all sessions in the process, 256 MB per script, 60 s wait) and whether a script blocks the root's turn while it runs or can run in the background; timeouts and limits; how results and errors return; how parentToolCallId scopes nested calls; any permission or sandbox controls on scripts.

result:
result: Codemode scripts can call any registered tool (extension tools included) and can run non-LLM models, but they cannot run chat models. Kimi's docs give no effort-level benchmarks or advice on when to use max. Evidence is from docs and sources dated Oct–Nov 2026. I fetched the 1.5.0 `codemode.md` directly. I read the other pi pages from pi.dev/docs/latest and the pi 1.4.0 changelog, so I did not check them against 1.5.0.

**Codemode (pi 1.5.0)**
- **What a script is:** the script is raw JavaScript run in a QuickJS sandbox, with no filesystem, network or timers. It reaches the outside only through `tools.<name>(args)` and `models`. [codemode.md](https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent@1.5.0/docs/codemode.md)
- **Modes:** `codemode.mode` is `on` (default) or `only`. With `on`, other tools stay declared to the model. With `only`, every active tool is hidden from the model and listed in the `codemode` description, so the model reaches everything through scripts. [codemode.md](https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent@1.5.0/docs/codemode.md), [settings](https://pi.dev/docs/latest/settings)
- **What `only` breaks:** the rpiv issue #310 report was that `ask_user_question` was no longer invoked under `only`. The fix in rpiv-ask-user-question 2.14.0 registers it with `exposure: "model-only"`, so the model calls it directly and scripts cannot call it. [CHANGELOG](https://github.com/juicesharp/rpiv-mono/blob/main/packages/rpiv-ask-user-question/CHANGELOG.md)
- **Which tools a script can call:** every tool the session can call is a method on `tools`. Extension tools follow the exposure values (see [Tools in Depth](https://programmer.ie/books/pi/17-chapter/), a third-party book; the [0.99.0 changelog](https://pi.dev/changelog/releases/0.99.0) confirms the five exposure values):
  - `direct` (default): callable while active.
  - `codemode`: callable whenever registered.
  - `deferred`: callable but not listed in the description.
  - `model-only` and `hidden`: never callable from a script.
  - `codemode` and `deferred` tools stay callable whether active or not ([extensions](https://pi.dev/docs/latest/extensions)).
  - Scripts find tools with `searchTools()`, `describeTool()` and `ALL_TOOLS`. [codemode.md](https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent@1.5.0/docs/codemode.md)
- **Subagents and models from a script:**
  - Chat models are listed but cannot be run from scripts. Only classifier and image models run, at most 4 at once per script. [codemode.md](https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent@1.5.0/docs/codemode.md)
  - A script can start a subagent only through an extension tool. Whether `pi-subagents`' `Agent` tool and `@aliou/pi-processes` tools are `direct` (so callable) is **unknown**; I did not read their registrations.
  - `Promise.all` and `Promise.allSettled` over tool calls are supported. [codemode.md](https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent@1.5.0/docs/codemode.md)
  - tintinweb/pi-subagents has its own `SubagentWorkflow` tool (`agent()`, `parallel()`, `pipeline()`). It runs in the background, claims to run Claude Code `Workflow` scripts unchanged, and disables itself if another extension provides a `Workflow` or `SubagentWorkflow` tool. [README](https://github.com/tintinweb/pi-subagents/)
  - `pi-ptc-subagents` offers `pi_task_codemode` inside codemode scripts. [package page](https://pi.dev/packages/pi-ptc-subagents)
- **Workers:** at most 2 workers are alive across all sessions in one process; `PI_CODEMODE_MAX_WORKERS` changes this. Each script gets 256 MB. At capacity, scripts queue in arrival order for up to 60 seconds (or until `timeout_ms`), then fail without running. A cancelled worker holds its slot until it exits. [Environment Variables](https://pi.dev/docs/latest/environment-variables), [codemode.md](https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent@1.5.0/docs/codemode.md)
- **Timeouts and limits:**
  - `// @options: {"max_output_tokens", "timeout_ms"}` must be the first line.
  - `timeout_ms` is a hard deadline for the whole script and is unset by default.
  - `max_output_tokens` defaults to 10000; the full text goes to a temp file.
  - Output is capped at 16777216 characters or 100000 `text()`, `image()` and `console` calls.
  - Scripts cannot start other `codemode` scripts.
  - A promise that can never settle fails immediately, since there are no timers. [codemode.md](https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent@1.5.0/docs/codemode.md)
- **Does a script block the root's turn:** the docs describe a script as one tool call that returns `Script completed` or `Script failed` with wall time. They document no background mode. **Unknown** whether anything else prevents blocking; it follows from the docs that the turn waits.
- **Results and errors:**
  - A failed call rejects with an `Error`.
  - Calls made before a failure are not undone.
  - Calls still running when the script ends are cancelled.
  - A failed script keeps its partial output followed by `Script error:`.
  - `store` and `load` persist small JSON values across `codemode` calls. [codemode.md](https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent@1.5.0/docs/codemode.md)
- **`parentToolCallId`:** nested calls emit `tool_call`, `tool_result` and `tool_execution_*` events carrying `parentToolCallId`. Their ids look like parent id / child. They add no transcript entries. A bounded `nestedCalls` record goes on the caller's result: at most 256 calls, with no results kept. Nested usage rolls up to the caller. [extensions](https://pi.dev/docs/latest/extensions), [Tools in Depth](https://programmer.ie/books/pi/17-chapter/)
- **Permissions and sandbox:** nested calls pass through `tool_call` handlers, so permission or guard extensions see them and can block them. I found no per-script permission setting. [Tools in Depth](https://programmer.ie/books/pi/17-chapter/), [pi-codemode-snippets](https://pi.dev/packages/pi-codemode-snippets)

**Kimi K3.1 Pro reasoning effort**
- **Levels and defaults:** the levels are `low`, `high` and `max`, and thinking cannot be turned off. The platform API defaults to `max`. The Kimi Code `k3.1-pro` model table says the default is `high`. The two sources conflict. [reasoning effort](https://platform.kimi.ai/docs/guide/use-reasoning-effort), [K3.1 quickstart](https://platform.kimi.ai/docs/guide/kimi-k3-1-pro-quickstart), [Kimi Code models](https://www.kimi.com/code/docs/en/kimi-code/models)
- **What each level changes:** Moonshot says the effort levels "balance reasoning depth, latency, and token usage". The only concrete guidance is that `low` reduces reasoning if it takes too long. No numbers per level: quality, latency, tokens and Kimi for Coding quota are **unknown**. [quickstart](https://platform.kimi.ai/docs/guide/kimi-k3-1-pro-quickstart)
- **Moonshot advice on when to use max:** none found. Moonshot's tool-calling guide only says to pick effort before the conversation starts. [tool-calling best practice](https://platform.kimi.ai/docs/guide/kimi-k3-tool-calling-best-practice)
- **Benchmarks by effort:** all published K3.1 Pro results use `max`, and no `low` or `high` scores were found. [HF model card](https://huggingface.co/moonshotai/Kimi-K3.1-Pro), [tech blog](https://www.kimi.ai/blog/kimi-k3-1-pro)
- **Session behavior:** changing effort mid-session invalidates the context cache and forces a new prefill. Moonshot says to keep it fixed and start a new session to change it. [Kimi Code models](https://www.kimi.com/code/docs/en/kimi-code/models)
- **Tool mapping:** Kimi Code maps `xhigh`, `ultra` and `max` to `max`, and `medium` and `high` to `high`. [Kimi Code models](https://www.kimi.com/code/docs/en/kimi-code/models)
- **Not asked but relevant:** `k3.1-pro-highspeed` is about 2-3x faster for about 2x quota. [Kimi Code models](https://www.kimi.com/code/docs/en/kimi-code/models)

- Measure `max` against `high` locally, since no vendor data exists.
